q: (Original MCQ #399) In which country is the Suez Canal?
facts: Connects: Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea. • Opened in: 1869. Located in: Egypt (continent: Africa).

q: (Original MCQ #404) Hazrat Hamza Martyred in?
facts: Hamza's title: “Asadullah” (Lion of Allah). Martyred in the Battle of Uhud by: Wahshi. His body was mutilated by: Hind bint Utbah.

q: (Original MCQ #407) Who was the first Pakistani to climb K2, and on what date did he summit it?
facts: Ashraf Aman made the first Pakistani ascent of K2 on 27 July 1977, in a joint expedition with Japan. K2 is the world's second-highest peak; the first is Mount Everest.
rel: First Pakistani woman to summit K2: Samina Baig (July 2022).

q: (Original MCQ #422) What is the stated range of Pakistan's Ababeel missile?
facts: Ababeel's stated range is about 2,200 km. Special capability MIRV (Multiple Independently targetable Reentry Vehicle) — Pakistan's first such missile. First tested in: January 2017. Developed by – NESCOM.

q: (Original MCQ #445) What was the codename of India's 1998 nuclear tests?
facts: India's 1998 tests (Pokhran-II) were codenamed Operation Shakti, conducted under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Pokhran-I (1974) was codenamed “Smiling Buddha.” Pakistan's response test: 1998 (Chagai-I).

q: (Original MCQ #454) Abu Jahal was Killed in Which Battle?
facts: Battle's year: 2 A.H (624 AD). Abu Jahal was killed by: Muadh ibn Amr and Muadh ibn Afra. Muslim commander at Badr: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

q: (Original MCQ #457) Muhammad Ali was the Boxer of?
facts: Muhammad Ali was an American boxer. Real name: Cassius Clay. Nickname: “The Greatest.” • Famous fight: “Rumble in the Jungle” (1974)

q: (Original MCQ #466) Asian Development Bank Headquarters?
facts: ADB headquarters: Manila, Philippines. ADB founded in: 1966. Pakistan's ADB membership: Founding member.
rel: ADB focuses on: Poverty reduction and development in Asia-Pacific.

q: (Original MCQ #567) Who received the Nishan-e-Haider for his service during the 1999 Kargil conflict?
facts: Havildar Lalak Jan was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for gallantry in the Kargil War (1999). • Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's – Highest military gallantry award. • Total Nishan-e-Haider recipients so far: 11.

q: (Original MCQ #580) “Hero of the Russian Federation” Medal Belongs to Which Country?
facts: Predecessor Soviet-era title Hero of the Soviet Union. Pakistan's equivalent highest award: Nishan-e-Haider. USA's highest military award – Medal of Honor.

q: (Original MCQ #610) City of Eight Bazaars?
facts: Faisalabad is called the "City of Eight Bazaars." Faisalabad's old name: Lyallpur. Also called “Manchester of Pakistan.” Famous local landmark: Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar).

q: (Original MCQ #661) How many faces does a triangular prism have?
facts: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. A cube has 6 faces.

q: (Original MCQ #677) “Hero of the Soviet Union” Medal was Introduced by Which Country?
opts: The Soviet Union (“Hero of the Soviet Union” medal)
facts: “Hero of the Soviet Union” was introduced by the Soviet Union in 1934. Modern Russian successor title: “Hero of the Russian Federation.” • Pakistan's equivalent highest award: Nishan-e-Haider.

q: (Original MCQ #691) Which city did Jenny Lind call “the Paradise of America” in 1851?
facts: Nickname coined by Opera singer Jenny Lind, in 1851. She called Northampton, Massachusetts: “The Paradise of America.” • Northampton is home to: Smith College.

q: (Original MCQ #697) Plants Absorb Nitrogen Mainly from?
facts: Plants absorb nitrogen mainly from the soil, as nitrates. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil convert nitrogen into a usable form. Nitrogen's share in the atmosphere — About 78%.

q: (Original MCQ #812) Which city is closest to Mohenjo-Daro?
facts: Mohenjo-daro is located in – Larkana District, Sindh, about 28 km from Larkana city. Belongs to: The Indus Valley Civilization. Discovered in 1922

q: (Original MCQ #826) Which Pass Connects Pakistan and Afghanistan?
facts: Khyber Pass specifically links Peshawar and Kabul. Length: About 53 km. Historically used by: Persians, Greeks, Mughals, British.

q: (Original MCQ #832) Bolan Pass Connects?
opts: Bolan Pass actually connects Quetta with Sibi and Jacobabad (toward the Indus plains)
facts: Located in: Balochistan. Connects Quetta with Sibi and Jacobabad (the Sindh plains). Historically used as a route to: Afghanistan (via Chaman). Length: About 89 km.

q: (Original MCQ #843) Nobel Prize is Given in How Many Fields?
facts: Six: Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economic Sciences. The 6th prize, Economic Sciences, was added in 1968 (first awarded 1969). Nobel Prizes are awarded annually in Stockholm and Oslo. Founded by: Alfred Nobel.
